portion_doctrine: Gary Vaynerchuk keynote on B2B premium services marketing. Distilled: Revenue follows brand/attention arbitrage, not lead-gen mechanics. Real ROI emerges over 4-6 years, not 90 days. Build reputation as primary asset; personal brand IS the moat. Conversion tactics fail without equity. Content production (scale/context) is the unscalable leverage point. Execution beats strategy; patience beats audacity in family/founder situations.
operating_rules: Content creation first, conversion second: give value 5x before asking once (jab/jab/jab/right hook model)
Spend 70% on proven platforms (Facebook, LinkedIn, direct mail); 10% on emerging; rest reserved. Not 20/60/20 split but 70/10/20 actual capital allocation.
Micro-target by geography + demographic + psychographic (e.g., 55-60 year old male in Chicago interested in 1986 Bears, not just 'Chicago males')
When scaling underpriced channels (Facebook Messenger at 87% open rate, Instagram Stories, YouTube pre-roll), squeeze maximum before moat collapses. Move dollars when medium saturates, not before.
One-on-one cadence: founders under 50 people must do direct 1:1s monthly+, asking what makes each person happy (work, title, money, time, meaning). Third meeting they reveal actual problems.
Influencer DM-blocking tactic: hire 1+ FTE at minimum wage to DM influencers 10 hrs/day until blocked on 40+ accounts, daily. Cyclical, not one-time.
Build reputation and legacy through teaching people how NOT to use you (anti-sell). Film free consultations, publish them, don't transact. Referral density follows.
Personal brand = context + consistency + time. Organic reach is PR/foundation (20% energy); paid distribution is business driver (80% budget). Do not reverse allocation.
Invest in unscalable work: hand-written notes, coffee meetings, direct DMs at 3am. These are the moat. Systemization kills differentiation at premium price points.
Autonomous decision-making gate for founder takeovers: agree on salary cap for parents, then founder makes all other decisions without veto. Remove emotion via macro clarity.

When 2+ businesses plateau, problem is always: switched from brand-building to lead-gen tactics, reduced content production volume, stopped being contextual. Solution: 3x content, shrink audience, add relevance layers.
named_methods: The 4-hour hand-to-hand combat method: spend 4-6 hours daily replying to people on Twitter/Instagram (2007-2011 playbook) in your niche. 0.2 cent social capital deposits compound. Only works 90+ days in.

Jab Jab Jab Right Hook: content discipline across platforms. Give value that has NOTHING to do with product before asking. Mix mediums (video, written, audio, meme) by platform affordance, not personal comfort.
Volume method for high-ticket closes: make 497 pieces of content targeting 15 people via micro-audience, overpay on CPM to reach exact psychographic. Close rate beats CPA optimization.

Wine Library TV model: act like PBS/editorial (Lifestyles of Rich and Famous), not QVC. Never stockpile inventory for on-air mentions. Separate content intent from sales intent. Repeatable on any DTC brand.

The mayor tactic: become mayor of your town. Deep local engagement on local Instagram photos, contextualized comments, 4-6 hours/day. Generates 4,000+ comments monthly. Works for real estate, local services, regional DMAs.

LinkedIn Moment discovery: platform is in Facebook 2012 moment. Organic reach is free still (no followers needed). Post thought-of-day about 22 years experience, use it as brand PR gateway to lead capture.
Franchisee as equity layer: offer long-tenured employees (5+ years) 50/50 ownership. You fund, they operate. Converts wage-earners into owners; solves scaling without dilution.

Messenger momentum window: 87-90% open rate on bot-sent links currently (live in 2019 tech moment). Unsustainable. Extract maximum while available. 30k list = 26k opens per send. Then pivot to email or next channel when rules change.
numbers: 70/10/20 budget split: 70% on proven channels (FB, LinkedIn, direct mail, Google), 10% on emerging (TikTok, Snapchat, new platforms), 20% operational reserve
22-second content daily: lawyer with 22 years experience posts 22-second thoughts daily on LinkedIn. Compound effect = unseemly personal brand gravitas over 6-12 months
497 pieces of content: volume threshold to close one high-ticket ($60k+) buyer via micro-targeting. Requires hyper-relevance + CPM overspend on wrong audiences to reach 15 right ones
4 to 8 hours daily: social engagement floor (2007-2011 Twitter model). Hand-to-hand combat baseline. Less than 4 hrs = vanity; 6-10 hrs = competitive edge
Third meeting reveal: in 1:1 cadence, first two meetings are surface-level. Third meeting is when employees/founders reveal actual constraints/desires/friction
87% open rate: Facebook Messenger current (2019 moment) for bot-sent links to free training. Unsustainable; capitalize while available
80% budget to paid distribution: if organic is PR gateway, 80% of content budget goes to running ads against owned audiences, not to creating organic content
60k price point: requires one-minute rants to 15 highly-specific micro-segments, each at high CPM waste to reach the 15 in a pool of 5,000. Volume + precision beats reach optimization

Two million to 10 million 3-year jump: requires: personal brand equity (18 months minimum), podcast + video team, influencer DM outreach (1 FTE daily), brand partnerships. No single tactic moves needle
50/50 equity offer: long-tenured employee owns 50% of franchise unit. You fund. Eliminates franchise quality-of-execution risk while scaling presence
specific_tactics: Real estate lead gen: search town name on Instagram Places, like/comment on every recent post with contextual knowledge. 4 hrs/day = 'mayor' status. Buyers research you before calling.

Micro-audience targeting cascade: pick 1 DMA (e.g., Malibu, Upper East Side African American males in tech), layer psychographics (Hermes fan, trust fund tier), add contextual reference (Abeza watch brand), shoot content for that cohort only. Repeat 20+ times.

Free consultation as content asset: film 10+ free calls per month. Publish 3-5 best ones per month on FB/LinkedIn. No testimonials (disbelieved); use educational/storytelling frame instead. Converts on trust not transaction pitch.

DM influencer block farming: hire scrappy junior (13 hrs/day, legal hours) to DM 40+ influencer accounts daily until blocked. Rotate new accounts. This is customer acquisition, not vanity. Non-obvious but compounding.

Product placement at scale: give product free to 100+ micro-YouTubers. Tell them upfront you'll run ads to their fans. 50% will appreciate, 50% may feel used. Transparency prevents reputation damage. Nike playbook (not original).
Wine-as-PDF not QVC: show wine/art as editorial interest, not transaction opportunity. Separates brand content from conversion pressure. Builds editorial moat; then customers approach you.
Coffee as conversion funnel: for $100k+ items, all digital should funnel to coffee meeting. No 'buy now' button. Friction is feature. Relationship closes, not copy.
One launch per quarter: release new product tier (e.g., $47 to $497 tier) quarterly. Measure LTV by tier. Evergreen ~100k; launch window ~250k in 4 days. Cycle prevents saturation.
Salary cap negotiation: in family business takeover, agree on founder salary number upfront. Everything else is founder's discretion. Removes emotional veto power. Accelerates growth 3-4x.
CEO hand-to-hand: personally respond to DMs/comments at 3am. Scale the unscalable. Every piece of written word on social is you. Creates moat; competitors can't replicate.
prompts: What is the actual decision-making bottleneck: Is it emotion, ideology, or lack of information? Frame the constraint in macro financial terms (salary cap, budget threshold) rather than subjective opinion.
Are you in the sales business or brand business? If you're launching quarterly and measuring CAC, you're in sales. Flip the ratio: 80% brand, 20% sales. Then watch CAC fall and LTV rise.
Who are the 15 people you actually want to close? What town do they live in, what brand do they follow, what age are they? Now overspend on CPM to reach 5,000 people in that DMA to hit those 15.
Can you film this and publish it? If the answer is no, you're not building a personal brand, you're transacting. Separate content (filmed, published) from commerce (private, consultative).
Are you squeezing the current channel or jumping to the next? If Messenger is 87% open rate, you don't need TikTok. Maximize current moat until it collapses, then transition.
What makes this employee actually happy in life? (Not job satisfaction score. Real life.) If the answer takes 3 meetings to surface, you haven't been listening in 1:1s.
If I gave you 10x the content production budget, would your business outcome change? If no, you don't have a content volume problem; you have a context/relevance problem.
tools: Instagram Places search + engagement farming (mayor tactic)
Twitter advanced search (keywords in niche) for hand-to-hand engagement
Facebook custom audience targeting (geographic + age + interests + pixel data)
Messenger bot + CRM integration for 87% open-rate sequences
Podcast sponsorships (pre-roll audio ads for niche audiences)
Email list segmentation by purchase intent (Evergreen vs Launch sequence)
YouTube pre-roll contextual targeting (search behavior retargeting)
LinkedIn organic posting (currently underpriced organic reach, Q1 2019)
Influencer DM outreach automation (rotating accounts, daily block farming)
skills: Contextual copywriting: adapt language/slang/references to micro-segment (don't say 'slut' to Upper East Side 84-year-old)
Personal brand reputation measurement: track owned-media engagement rate, DM inquiries, organic referral attribution over 6-12 months
Founder psychology: recognize when takeover bottleneck is emotional (stealing $500/mo, overreacting) vs structural (no autonomy, no cap agreement)
Channel life-cycle reading: identify when a platform is in early arbitrage phase (YouTube pre-roll 2018, Messenger 2019) vs saturation (Facebook 2015). Know when to squeeze vs pivot.
Micro-audience construction: layer demographic, psychographic, contextual signals to identify 15-person bullseye in 50k DMA pool
Content intent separation: understand editorial (build trust, no ask) vs transactional (ask for sale). Never mix in same piece.
Hand-to-hand combat patience: accept 90+ day runway before volume compounds. Quit within 13 days = why 1% execute.
gates: Family business takeover gate: founder must get explicit salary agreement from parent/partner. Without cap, emotional veto power persists. Gate fails if founder accepts 'we'll figure it out'
Content volume gate: if producing <30 pieces/week across platforms, you're not in the brand-building phase yet. Don't measure CAC until volume hits 100+/week.
Channel saturation gate: before pivoting from Messenger/Stories/Pre-roll, measure current CPM weekly. Only pivot when CPM increases 3x or open rate drops below 40%.
Personal brand gate: if you can't publish it, it doesn't count. Unpublished advice/thoughts don't compound into reputation equity.
1:1 cadence gate: hire freeze until founder has completed 1:1s with every employee asking 'what makes you happy?' Third meeting reveals truth. Don't hire before this clarity.
Influencer transparency gate: if running ads to influencer's fan base, disclose upfront. 50% will accept; 50% may feel used. Transparency prevents 'used me' narrative later.
content_ideas: Attorney Q&A show: lawyer answers 4 legal questions/week from LinkedIn audience. Format: 10-min video per question. Positions as educator, not closer.
Free consultation film library: capture 10 consultations/month, publish 3-5 best as educational case studies. No testimonials, no closing pitch. Pure advice.
22-second daily: lawyer/service provider posts 22-second thought on 22 years experience daily. Compound over 12 months = authority in niche.
Town-specific Instagram engagement: DM/comment on every recent photo in your service area (real estate, local legal, local service). Become 'mayor' of the DMA.

Podcast interview series: 'Colorado Helping Professionals' podcast. Weekly interview with one niche service provider (lawyer, CPA, therapist) in your area. 400-person hyper-local audience grows referral density.

Micro-segment video series: create 5 versions of same offer (e.g., personal injury case strategy) targeting different micro-segments (retirees, young families, business owners). Different tone, reference, pain-point framing per segment.
Behind-the-scenes operations: taco shop owner publishes weekly story about sourcing, training, scaling 13 shops. Not product placement; brand mythology. Builds founder-as-category-owner narrative.
Competitor 'love' content: review a competing artist/gallery video. Give genuine praise. Position self as whisperer to the category, not seller.
Before-and-after founder story: film your failure arc (2008 crash, 50% revenue loss, rebuilding). Publish as long-form (20 min video or podcast). Generic and replicable to any founder.
contradictions: Organic reach investment vs paid allocation reversal: Gary says LinkedIn organic is 'free' and posts without followers get 1k+ reach, but also says 80% of budget should go to paid distribution. If organic is so cheap, why not 50/50? Answer: organic is brand/PR layering (20%), paid is revenue driver (80%). Most entrepreneurs reverse this.

Messenger as growth channel vs platform risk: Gary advocates squeezing Messenger at 87% open rate while platform has 30k list, but warns against over-reliance on single channels. Tension: if you build 30k Messenger list and Facebook changes rules (likely), you lose everything. Mitigation: extract list to email + SMS simultaneously (offload risk). Not mentioned explicitly.

Founder autonomy vs parent respect in family business: Gary advises son to demand full operational autonomy from father, but also warns against audacity and lack of patience for founders taking over. Tensions unresolved: at what point does founder get full autonomy vs waiting parent out? When do you override parent wisdom vs defer? Gary's answer: salary cap agreement removes emotion, but assumes parent's non-financial concerns (brand integrity, legacy) don't resurface.

Content volume as moat vs content quality/context: Gary emphasizes 497 pieces of content to close 1 high-ticket customer, but also stresses contextual relevance and intent. Implication: raw volume without context = spam. But high-context content takes longer to produce. Trade-off unresolved: volume or context first? Answer appears to be: volume provides A/B testing feedback to refine context, so volume THEN context. But most practitioners do context-less volume.

Personal brand as business risk vs essential moat: Gary built Vaynermedia on reputation; clients want him personally. But this creates key-person risk. What happens when founder steps back? Gary acknowledges the contradiction (either charge 5x for associates, or don't take the work), but doesn't resolve. Is personal brand scaling or scaling-blocking?
weird_gold: The 0.2 cent deposit theory: every comment/like on someone's Instagram post costs you $0.002 in attention capital. Over 90 days of 4-6 hrs/day, at 90 comments/day, you've spent $1.80 in capital to become known in a town. Weird but non-zero. Most people can't think small-scale enough.

Myspace exit strategy: Gary reminds audience that every platform dies (Myspace to Facebook shift). The people most pot-committed to Instagram right now will panic when it fades. He'd 'laugh' if Instagram disappeared because he's diversified. Weird psychological frame: celebrate the death of your current distribution. Builds resilience.

Wine Library TV reverse learnings: Gary planned to do QVC-style (sell wine on air), but when camera went on, realized he'd rather be PBS/editorial (Lifestyles of Rich and Famous). This single creative reorientation changed the outcome from another shopping network to a 1,000-episode educational phenomenon. The weird insight: your format decision matters more than your traffic.

Franchisee as parent payback mechanism: offer long-tenured employees 50/50 ownership with you funding. They now have equity, you now have expansion. Taco guy could 50/50 20 employees into 20 franchises, making them mini-CEOs. Solves both hiring retention and scaling. Weird because it's not about hiring, it's about ownership distribution as leverage.

The 1:1 reveal lag time: first one-on-one reveals nothing. Second reveals less. Third meeting is when people actually tell you what's wrong (with them, the job, the culture). This implies: if you've only been doing monthly 1:1s for 2 months, you haven't diagnosed anything. Minimum 3-4 months to understand reality. Weird because it suggests most company cultures are built on incomplete information.

Supreme shoes as failed investment: Gary bought an apartment 6 months before he could have gone all-in on Uber and doubled his liquidity. He regrets this. Weird insight: owning a home reduced flexibility and cost him potential Uber/Stripe/early-scale investments. He now thinks nobody should own a home until 40+ if they have founder ambitions. Highly contrarian but quantified.

Facebook Messenger warm-takes strategy: send Messenger DMs with 87% open rate, 30k list, 1-click follow-through. But 17k people complained about unsolicited messages and got warned by Facebook. He downplays it ('they got into Messenger the wrong way'). Weird: building on borrowed platforms with 30k names is fragile. He knows this. Continues anyway.

The 50% influencer acceptance rate: if you give micro-YouTubers free product and run ads against their fans without disclosure, 50% appreciate the distribution, 50% feel used. He advocates transparency upfront. Weird implication: 1 out of 2 partnership attempts will have tension. This is normalized as 'the cost of scaling'.

Ed's $5-6 figure/month Facebook ad spend with 90% negative reviews = growing leads: Gary's insight is that people don't believe reviews as much as we think. So Ed running negative-comment Facebook ads (high attention, high reach) still pulls leads because the attention signal matters more than comment sentiment. Weird: bad PR is still PR if it's visible enough.

Your people are not your business: when Gary tells the taco guy to franchise long-tenured employees into ownership, he's saying 'Susan's taco quality matters more than your process.' Yet earlier he said 'build systems not people.' Contradiction unresolved: is the moat people or process? Answer seems to be: early stage = people. Franchise/scale = process + people trust = ownership alignment.
